newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM: tensions should not delay ASEAN bid.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM: tensions should not delay ASEAN bid.

text.p: Cambodian Co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh said on Friday that political tensions should not be allowed to delay the country's bid for ASEAN membership in July 1997.

"The political tensions of Cambodia of course exist, but it is no reason to delay entering into ASEAN," the first prime minister told reporters before departing for Saturday's Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in Jakarta.

Ranariddh said he expected ASEAN members would advise him on resolving friction between himself and Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, but asked that member nations leave Cambodia to sort out its internal conflicts.
"Please trust us to solve our problems. In fact, they are not serious, and in the future, there will be political stability in the Kingdom of Cambodia," he said.
Hun Sen is also attending the summit and both premiers are expected to return on Sunday.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. Cambodia, Laos and Burma are attending the meeting for the first time as observers.
There had been some question whether Ranariddh would attend the ASEAN meeting, with a local newspaper reporting this week that the disputes might keep him at home.

Tension between the co-premiers, who formed a shaky coalition government after U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993, has risen in recent months over power-sharing, land disputes and recruitment of Khmer Rouge guerrilla defectors to their separate camps.

The situation worsened last week with the murder of Hun Sen's brother-in-law and a political skirmish in the northwest city of Battambang. The killing of Hun Sen's relative is suspected to have been politically motivated, officials have said.
